verified.title: _batches_with_epoch_end flags every logical-minibatch boundary as an epoch end, so train.accum never takes effect and validation runs once per minibatch
verified.detail:
The helper's own docstring says it marks "the last physical block of the last logical minibatch the iterator yields", which is `nxt is None`. The expression is `is_epoch_end = nxt is None or nxt["mb"] != prev["mb"]`, and `mb` increments once per logical minibatch (train/methods/ctool.py:201-204, one integer per minibatch, consecutive blocks sharing it), so the flag is True at every minibatch boundary.

The flag is used twice. At line 277, `if len(seen_mbs) >= cfg.train.accum or is_epoch_end:` fires the optimizer step, so a step is taken after every single logical minibatch and `cfg.train.accum` is dead (its only remaining effect is line 272's `/ cfg.train.accum`, which now divides a one-minibatch gradient). Because `steps` is still computed as `ceil(ceil(n_train_events / events_per_mb) / accum) * epochs` (lines 193-196), the run hits its step budget after 1/accum of the planned minibatches and breaks at line 308-309: with the schema default `accum: 2` (experimental_settings/schema.py:109) every run trains on half the training split it was told to train on, per epoch, silently.

At line 303, `if is_epoch_end: _validate_and_maybe_save(ep)` runs `method.validate` over the whole val split after every logical minibatch instead of once per epoch. That contradicts the owner's ruling recorded in .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md ("2.6 (validate's cadence): ruled — validation runs once at every epoch end (plus once at the end when train.max_steps cut the last epoch short)"). For cgen and cparam each such call also runs GEN_N = 200 greedy generations (train/methods/cgen.py:28,303), so a real generator training would spend nearly all its GPU time validating.

This is a regression from fix round 1 (commit 27485a0, finding F2): the pre-fix code at 1e4645f had `is_epoch_end = (mb + 1) == m_per_epoch` (true only for the last minibatch), whose real bug was failing to fire when a method dropped events. The replacement overshot the target.

verified.title: Training runs with the backbone in eval mode whenever the alignment gate is skipped, which includes every resume; grad_ckpt silently becomes a no-op
verified.detail:
`trainer.run` never calls `probe.set_training(True)` on its own. The only two calls that enable training mode are the alignment gate's `finally` (line 374) and the restore after a validation (line 240). `base.load` returns the probe in eval mode: it builds the backbone with `AutoModel.from_pretrained` / `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained` (models/probe_models/base.py:199-202), and transformers' `from_pretrained` ends with `model.eval()` (external/probe-env/.../transformers/modeling_utils.py:4458).

The gate is guarded by `if cfg.train.align_check and resume_step is None:` (line 206). So two paths reach the step loop with the model still in eval mode: a setting with `align_check: false` (a documented field, schema.py:112), and **every resume**, whatever the setting says. With the default `epochs: 1` the model then stays in eval mode for the whole remaining run, because the next `set_training(True)` only comes after the first validation.

Consequence beyond dropout: transformers only checkpoints activations when the module is in training mode (`if self.gradient_checkpointing and self.training:`, transformers/modeling_layers.py:77). `probe.grad_checkpointing(True)` (line 178-179, from `cfg.train.grad_ckpt`) is therefore a silent no-op on those paths, so a resumed run needs the memory the flag exists to save -- on exactly the big-backbone runs where a crash-and-resume is likely (GPU acceptance item 3).

On the normal path the last beat carries `done == total`, and `registry.judge` returns `"done"` as its first rule (jobs/registry.py:662), so the monitor reports a train piece finished while it still has the whole prediction pass to run.

Contracts 8.4 requires every piece to emit `emit(0, total, unit)` before its main loop, and `registry.judge` on a piece with no beat compares its age against `DEFAULTS["warmup_s"] = 1800`, returning "suspected stall" after 30 minutes and escalating past 90 (`escalate_line = 3`).

refuted.title: The predict-only continuation writes done.json metrics holding only objective, dropping the validation extras the same key's uninterrupted run records
refuted.reason: The repro does reproduce (full run writes {'objective': 0.5, 'val_wacc': 0.5, 'val_lastcut_acc': 0.5}, predict-only writes {'objective': 0.5}), and run.py/registry.py do fold done.json metrics into the finish row and RESULTS.md's numbers column. But it is not a defect against the governing text. Ticket 13 step 11 pins train_done.json as exactly {key, commit, steps, best_objective, finished_at}, and contracts 1.6 pins best/meta.json as {backbone, tuning, labels, call_sep, param_only, max_len, train_key}; step 3 sends the predict-only path into step 11 with ckpt_dir = run_dir/"best", so those two files are the entire state it inherits and neither carries the validation extras. {"objective": train_done["best_objective"]} at trainer.py:329 is therefore the complete set of validation numbers the ticket's own handoff makes available -- the loss follows from the pinned design, not from a deviation. Contracts 1.5 defines train's metrics as "the best validation objective", which both paths write with the same value; contracts 2.4's row for this state asks only for "load best/, run the prediction step only, write predictions and done.json" and never requires the two done.json files to match; no errata entry (I checked the last ten and every metrics hit in contract-errata.md) touches train's metrics. The reviewer's implied source, train_log.jsonl, is not among the trainer's contracted reads (the continue rule names it only as a refusal marker) and reconstruction from it is ill-defined: best/best_metrics are per incarnation while the log is appended across incarnations, so a min-over-eval-lines could attach one incarnation's extras to another's recorded best_objective -- an absent number traded for a wrong one. verified.title: _batches_with_epoch_end reports the end of every logical minibatch as the end of the epoch, so gradient accumulation never accumulates and the run stops after 1/accum of the data
verified.detail:
trainer.py:108 computes `is_epoch_end = nxt is None or nxt["mb"] != prev["mb"]`. `nxt["mb"] != prev["mb"]` is true at *every* logical-minibatch boundary, not only at the last one, so the flag means "last physical block of this minibatch", which is what the docstring at :100-104 and the T13 report (line 179, describing the fix-round-1 change for F2) both claim is "true end-of-epoch". Three consequences, all with the shipped defaults (`experimental_settings/schema.py:109 accum: int = 2`, :104 `epochs: int = 1`):
1. trainer.py:277 `if len(seen_mbs) >= cfg.train.accum or is_epoch_end:` fires an `opt.step()`/`zero_grad()` after every single minibatch, so `accum` never accumulates anything and each step's gradient is also scaled down by `1/accum` at :272.
2. `steps` at :195-196 is still `ceil(ceil(n_events/events_per_mb)/accum) * epochs`, but `gstep` now increments once per minibatch, so the `if gstep >= steps: break` at :308 stops the run after `steps` minibatches -- exactly `1/accum` of the intended training data. The remaining events get no gradient at all, in any epoch (the `for ep` loop at :251 breaks immediately on the next epoch).
3. trainer.py:303-305 runs `method.validate` + a possible `best/` save after *every* minibatch instead of once per epoch. For cgen/cparam that is a full packed CE pass over the val split plus `GEN_N = 200` greedy generations per minibatch.
The correct condition for "the end of the epoch" on this one-item lookahead is `nxt is None` alone.
Why no acceptance command catches it: A3.4/A3.5 and tests/test_packed_loss.py all use `accum=1`, where `len(seen_mbs) >= 1` is already true at every minibatch, so the flag changes nothing there.
verified.repro:

  actual opt.step() calls: 4
  validate() calls: 4          <- should be 1 (one epoch)

verified.title: reference_loss scores rows that batches() legitimately drops (and truncates where batches() does not), so the alignment gate exits the run non-zero on correct packing
verified.file: train/methods/ctool.py:61-63 and :215-233; train/methods/cgen.py:61-63, :74-76 and :247-250; train/methods/cparam.py:76-78, :93-95 and :271-274
verified.detail:
`_run_alignment_gate` (trainer.py:359-387) compares `sum(method.loss(...) for method.batches(slice_df, ...))` against `method.reference_loss(probe, slice_df)`, both divided by `slice_df.height`, and raises SystemExit above 1e-4. `batches()` drops rows; `reference_loss` does not drop the same rows, and applies a different length policy. Three concrete divergences, none of them a packing bug:
(a) all three methods: `_build_events` drops an event whole when its longest text exceeds `cfg.train.max_len` (ctool:61-63, cgen:61-63, cparam:76-78 -- the errata rule that `done.json`'s `counts.dropped_overlong` exists to record), while `reference_loss` tokenizes every row of the frame with `truncation=False` and scores them all.
(b) cgen/cparam: `reference_loss` left-truncates the prompt to `max_len - len(tgt_ids)` (cgen:247-250, cparam:271-274, the legacy `collate` behaviour the ticket pins), while the packed path never truncates -- it only drops whole events over `max_len`. Any event whose longest text lands in the band `[max_len - len(call_sep) - len(tgt), max_len]` is kept by one path and truncated by the other.
(c) cgen/cparam: a row whose target exceeds `MAX_TGT_TOK = 160` is dropped by `_build_events` (cgen:74-76, cparam:93-95) and kept by `reference_loss`.
The gate slice is the first `events_per_mb * accum` rows of the train split in `example_id` order -- 8 rows with the shipped defaults -- so whether the run survives is decided by whichever rows happen to sort first, and one affected row is enough. The packing itself is correct: I could not make packed and plain diverge on any row shape (empty tail, non-prefix row, several events per block, an event over the block budget); every failure I produced comes from the drop/truncation asymmetry, not from the mask or the positions.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED, with one sub-part discounted as ticket-prescribed.

Reproduced at df3c473 against a `git archive` export, driven through the shipped gate (`train/utils/trainer.py:359-387`, `_run_alignment_gate`), not a hand-rolled comparison: harness `/tmp/pk03_gate.py` plus `/tmp/pk03_slice.py`. Control (the A3.3 fixture) passes: ctool diff 0.000e+00, cgen/cparam 1.272e-06. The three divergences all raise SystemExit with "the packing in <method>.batches has a bug": (a) overlong event at max_len=64 -> ctool 6.474e-01, cgen 6.122e+00, cparam 6.055e+00; (b) truncation band (longest 97 tok, text+sep 101, target 7, max_len=99) -> cgen 6.919e-03, cparam 1.525e-02; (c) a cgen target of 583 tokens over MAX_TGT_TOK=160 -> 3.966e+00. I also ran the shape the shipped defaults actually produce (events_per_mb=4 * accum=2 = 8 rows, and 8 rows by example_id are the cuts of ONE event, since example_id is f"{task}__s{seed}|s{step}|c{cut}"): when that one event is over max_len, packed = 0.0 against plain 0.886 (ctool) / 11.98 (cgen) / 11.74 (cparam).

Mechanism confirmed in the code: `_build_events` drops an event whole when its longest text exceeds cfg.train.max_len (train/methods/ctool.py:61-63, cgen.py:61-63, cparam.py:76-78) and drops a row whose target exceeds MAX_TGT_TOK (cgen.py:74-76, cparam.py:93-95), while `reference_loss` tokenizes every row of the frame with truncation=False and scores them all (ctool.py:215-233, cgen.py:239-250, cparam.py:263-274). `trainer.py:181` hands the gate the unfiltered train split and `:362` slices `train_df.sort("example_id").head(n)`; nothing pre-filters, and both sides are divided by slice_df.height regardless of drops. probe.max_len equals cfg.train.max_len (models/probe_models/base.py:190), so the (b) band is real and not an artefact of two different limits.

Why it is a defect and not prescribed: contracts 2.6's hook table pins `reference_loss` as "the same loss computed one example row per sequence, in its plainest form, over a slice of the same example-row frame trainer.run hands batches", and 2.5 makes the gate stop training above 1e-4; ticket 13's A3.3 says "a diff above the tolerance is the packing bug the gate exists for". The drops themselves are prescribed (errata line 118, "a longer event is dropped whole ... the count is done.json's counts.dropped_overlong"; ticket section 3 for MAX_TGT_TOK), but nothing in the ticket or errata prescribes that `reference_loss` scores rows batches drops -- the ctool text says "the same number", and filtering the reference to the rows batches keeps was available. So cases (a) and (c) are an implementation choice that breaks the gate's premise and makes a correct run exit non-zero with a message that misattributes the cause. Case (b) I discount: ticket 13 explicitly pins the left-truncated legacy collate for cgen/cparam's reference_loss AND the drop-whole-no-truncation rule for batches, so the band divergence follows from two explicit ticket sentences (a spec conflict, worth the owner's eye, not an implementer defect).

Not a duplicate: the wave-5 records list a dropped_overlong concern (counts.dropped_overlong is train-split-only) and F6/N1, none of which is this.

Severity: important rather than critical, and the reviewer's own framing slightly overstates reachability. The failure is a visible hard stop before the first optimizer step, recoverable with train.align_check: false or a larger max_len, not a silent wrong number. With the shipped defaults the 8-row slice is the first step of the alphabetically first train task -- the shortest context and the smallest call in the dataset -- so at max_len 8192 an affected row landing there is unlikely; it becomes likely as soon as max_len is lowered to fit a card, and then the whole slice drops and the gate reports packed=0 as a packing bug.

refuted.title: cparam re-evaluates ASSEMBLY_MISMATCH_LIMIT on every _build_events call, so one unassembled row inside the 8-row alignment-gate slice kills a run whose real mismatch rate is far under the limit
refuted.reason:
The repro reproduces mechanically (SystemExit "1/8 = 0.125 exceeds 0.05" on the 8-row gate slice, run from a git archive df3c473 export with probe-env python), but the finding fails on both its rule premise and its reachability premise.

(1) Its central claim about legacy is wrong. The hard stop lives inside legacy's load_events (legacy/pipeline/train/share_data.py:330-344), and load_events is called on the train split (train_causal_share.py:1067), the val split (:1070), the mem-probe reload (:1153) AND legacy's own alignment gate (:767-778), which samples --align-events val events (default 6, :991) into a temp file via _align_candidates/_write_align_tmpfile and calls load_events(tmp_path, tok, mode="cparam", ...) on it. Legacy therefore evaluated the same ratio on its own small alignment subset; per-frame evaluation is legacy's behaviour, not a deviation from it.

(2) Ticket 13:353-355 says only that mismatching rows "are dropped whole and counted as assembly_mismatch, and the file raises when their share exceeds ASSEMBLY_MISMATCH_LIMIT"; it pins no denominator scope, and no errata entry touches it (grep over contract-errata.md finds only the cparam separator entry 114 and the cparam-setting entry 125). The implementation is the literal reading of the rule.

(3) The failure scenario is unreachable from this tree's data. The only writer of examples.parquet is data/build_training_dataset.py:279; each row's call is env.build_call(tool, call_args), which is f"{tool}({', '.join(parts)})" (data/environments/appworld.py:313-318), and any event whose call build_call refuses or that fails the split_args round-trip gate is skipped before a row is written (build_training_dataset.py:177-205). So call.startswith(tool + "(") holds for every row a build emits and assembly_mismatch is structurally zero. A genuine assembly drift changes the prefix for every row, so it fires on the whole train frame and whole val frame as well; the drift alarm keeps its meaning. The reviewer's "real rate far under the limit" needs a hand-built row ("TRANSFER phone.pay(id=1)") that no stage of this tree can produce.

(4) The secondary denominator point is legacy's own composition: legacy's tot = n_rows + assembly_mismatch, n_rows counts only kept rows, MAX_TGT_TOK drops are excluded from both numerator and denominator, and overlong events are dropped before the row loop (share_data.py:250-302, :330-344) -- identical to cparam.py:82-112, including the check order (mismatch first, then the target-length cap).

refuted.title: The walk's claim release is not fail-closed on an unreachable host: it deletes the records of pieces it then calls alive
refuted.reason:
Not a wave-5 defect. Three independent reasons.

1) The stated trigger is unreachable. The finding says a timed-out ssh deletes "the in-progress record files of live pieces" on the unreachable host. No record-owning process ever runs on an ssh-reached host: the only caller of `open_record` and the only writer of `owner_session` is `agent/run_tasks.py` (:19, :55, :125), which runs only as a `loop` piece, and `jobs/launch.py:760-767` gives every `loop` piece `host = _login_host()` unconditionally; `schema.STAGES["sample"]["pieces"]` / `["inject"]["pieces"]` (experimental_settings/schema.py:203-204, 277-278) are loop + service_agent + service_probe, with no `train` piece, and service pieces own no record files. The login host is probed with a local `bash -c`, not ssh (contract-errata entry "8.0 / 3.4 (`registry.session_alive` and `live_sessions`)"). The repro's premise -- `{"kind": "loop", "host": "tokyo106"}` -- is a placement the launcher cannot produce, so a remote host in `failed_hosts` removes no live loop session from the name set.

2) The behaviour is explicitly prescribed. Ticket 14 step 4 pins the call verbatim: "release the dead sessions' claims through `trajectory_record.release(run_dir, registry.live_sessions(), registry.DEFAULTS["launch_timeout_s"])`, report them, and launch nothing". run.py:732-733 is that call with those three arguments; the proposed fix replaces the pinned second argument. The order (release first, then the alive test) is the F1 fix recorded in T14-report.md:429-486 and adjudicated at merge.

3) The residual is pre-existing code outside the diff. What I did reproduce (/tmp/walkchk_release_check.py, external/probe-env/bin/python): `piece_alive: True` / `release deleted: ['task_9__s42.jsonl']`, and the same with the login host itself in `failed_hosts` (`login host recorded on a loop piece: shiga`, `piece_alive: True`, `release deleted: ['task_10__s42.jsonl']`). So the only live trigger left is the login machine's own probe failing -- a wedged tmux server or the 20 s `bash -c` timeout -- not an ssh timeout. That divergence is inherent to `release`'s pinned signature: contracts 1.1's offered-functions row fixes `release(dir, live_sessions, unowned_age_s)` over a bare set of session names, which cannot express host reachability, while fail-closedness lives in `_ProbedSessions.failed_hosts` and needs a host. `data/trajectory_record.release` and `jobs/registry.live_sessions` are ticket-03 code: `git diff --stat f520b87..df3c473` touches run.py, jobs/launch.py (the two names made public), README.md, train/*, tests/test_packed_loss.py -- neither file. At most this is a latent contracts-level gap for the owner (make `release` take the probe result, or have run.py add the sessions of pieces whose host is in `failed_hosts`), not an important defect in the wave-5 merge.

refuted.reason:
REFUTED. The behaviour reproduces, but no ticket/contract/errata text prescribes the frozen request, and the fix the finding proposes rests on a false premise about what `settings.yaml` holds.

Repro (git archive of df3c473 into /tmp, probe-env python, fake run dir under /tmp, nothing in the repo touched): I froze a `sample` directory with its own narrower request (split [train], n_tasks 2, seeds [42,67] = 4 pairs, `max_steps` 11 so the key differs from today's file), wrote a done record for all 4 pairs, and called `run._compute_progress` on a row pointing at it:
  the run's own request: 4 pairs, done under its own request: 4/4
  _compute_edited: {'sample-deadbeef0000': True}
  _compute_progress (what ls prints): (2, 315)
  what load_frozen would give: (4, 4)
So the effect is real and stronger than the reviewer's `0/315`: a complete run prints `2/315`. (The reviewer's "the numerator is the old run's records" is wrong, though — `done_pairs(dir, pairs)` returns the intersection with the passed list, so both halves are today's request.)

Why it is not a defect:

1. Nothing pins the source. Ticket 14 section 3 says only "`progress` (`trajectory_record.done_pairs` against the requested total)". Contracts 8.0 (the `ls` row) says the pair is "the per-`run_id` `(done, total)` that `run.py` computes with `data/trajectory_record.done_pairs`", and the reason given is that `registry.py` "cannot tell a done record from a claimed one" — not where the total comes from. 8.6's "the start row used only for the launch time and the frozen request" is about the meta.json/start-row split for host and session; the start row (8.1 field table) carries no (task, seed) count at all, and 8.6 sources progress from "the `progress` pair for a claiming stage". No errata entry touches it (grep for progress/done_pairs in contract-errata.md returns only the 1.1 `dir` entries).

2. `schema.load_frozen(run_dir)` does not give "the request that run froze". Contracts 3.4 makes the non-keyed request fields merge per field on every re-freeze of the same directory ("`seeds` becomes the ordered union of the two lists"), implemented as `_merge_request_fields` at experimental_settings/schema.py:1401, because one directory is reachable from several settings on purpose. I verified it: freezing owner A (seeds [42]) then owner B (seeds [67]) into one directory leaves `seeds: [42, 67]` with the key unchanged. So the frozen request is the widest request any owner ever made against that directory; for 9(c)#6's six sweep children sharing one sample directory, the proposed fix would print one union total on every child's row.

3. The implemented source matches the walk and the pieces. `_compute_progress` (run.py:254-282) issues the identical `open_env` + `requested_pairs` + `done_pairs` call the walk's skip test issues (run.py:703-709), so for every row whose key still matches, `ls`'s fraction is exactly the completeness the walk will act on — including 2.3's flagship "ask for a fourth seed" case, where seeds are not keyed, the row is not `edited`, and the frozen reading would print a misleading `100/100` for a run the walk is about to relaunch. For a live run the frozen and current requests are equal, so contracts 8.4's "the count of done record files in the directory against that one total" holds. The divergence exists only on a row the `edited` flag already marks as keying elsewhere.

4. The efficiency half is not a defect: 8.4 requires the done-record count for claiming stages, and I measured `_compute_progress` at 0.022-0.024 s per row (315 pairs, local disk), i.e. ~0.5 s for 20 rows, against the per-host `ssh tmux ls` `ls` already issues.

verified.title: trainer.run steps the optimizer at every logical minibatch, so train.accum is ignored and the epoch ends after a fraction of the data
verified.detail: _batches_with_epoch_end sets `is_epoch_end = nxt is None or nxt["mb"] != prev["mb"]`, which is true at the end of *every* logical minibatch, not at the end of the epoch (its own docstring says 'the last physical block of the last logical minibatch the iterator yields', which is just `nxt is None`). Both consumers then misfire. (a) The step gate `if len(seen_mbs) >= cfg.train.accum or is_epoch_end` takes an optimizer step at every minibatch boundary regardless of accum, while the gradient is still divided by accum; and because `seen_mbs.add(mb)` happens on the *first* physical block of a minibatch, the gate can also fire before that minibatch's remaining blocks have been accumulated. (b) `steps` was planned as ceil(m_per_epoch/accum)*epochs, so gstep reaches `steps` after m_per_epoch/accum minibatches and the `if gstep >= steps: break` ends training there -- with the schema default train.accum = 2 a run trains on half its examples, with accum = 3 on a third, and epochs > 1 never reaches the second epoch. (c) `if is_epoch_end: _validate_and_maybe_save(ep)` runs a full validation at every minibatch instead of once per epoch -- for cgen/cparam that is GEN_N = 200 greedy generations plus the whole val CE per minibatch. Every CPU acceptance command hides this: A3.4 uses accum=1 with 2 events_per_mb and 4 events, where one minibatch is exactly one block and the miscount is invisible.
verified.repro:
An A3.4 fixture with ACCUM/EVENTS/EPOCHS knobs (/tmp/seams/a34.py, same stubs as A3.4, align_check off, counting wrappers on ctool.loss and AdamW.step), run from an export of df3c473 with the probe venv:

ACCUM=1 EVENTS=8 EPMB=4 MAXLEN=48 (a minibatch that spans 2 physical blocks) -> 'one epoch: 2 logical minibatches, 4 physical blocks', 'loss() calls: 2 of 4', 'distinct minibatches trained on: 1 of 2'.

verified.title: Every method builds its label/weight tensors on the CPU while Probe.forward returns logits on the run's device, so the first GPU train dies in the alignment gate

verified.title: run.py never folds done.json's stage_extra into meta.json, so every eval stage raises KeyError('labels')
verified.detail: trainer.run puts the class order in its own done.json through registry.write_done(..., stage_extra={"labels": labels}) (trainer.py:350-355), which is exactly what contracts 8.3 prescribes: 'stage_extra | a free object; train puts the class order (labels) there. The stage writes it into its own done.json and run.py folds it in here [meta.json] on its walk (1.3), so this file keeps exactly two writers' (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:4525). eval/utils/probe_eval.py:579 reads it from the other side: `labels = train_meta["stage_extra"]["labels"]`, train_meta being the train directory's meta.json. run.py performs no such fold anywhere -- the string `stage_extra` does not occur in run.py, and none of its three registry.write_meta calls (lines 550, 690, 755) passes it, nor does jobs/launch.py or registry.sync(). registry._default_meta() seeds `"stage_extra": {}`, so the read raises KeyError rather than returning None. Consequence: after a train stage finishes, the walk's next stage (eval, a CPU stage spawned in place) exits non-zero and run.py appends a `failed` finish row; this blocks the ctool and the generator eval paths alike.

verdict.reason: CONFIRMED, could not refute. Contracts 1.3 (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:1232) and 8.3 (:4525) both prescribe that run.py folds done.json's stage_extra into the run's meta.json on the same walk that writes the finish row, and ticket 14's walk section names 8.2/8.3 as governing, so the fold is in ticket 14's file. run.py at df3c473 performs no fold: the string stage_extra does not occur in run.py, none of its write_meta calls (lines 550, 690, 755) passes it, jobs/launch.py:864 does not, and registry.sync() (jobs/registry.py:988-1030) folds only counts/metrics/report into finish rows. trainer.py:350-355 writes stage_extra={"labels": labels} into its own done.json exactly as ticket 13 line 156 pins, and eval/utils/probe_eval.py:579 reads train_meta["stage_extra"]["labels"] from the train dir's meta.json exactly as ticket 08 line 67 pins, with no default; registry._default_meta() seeds "stage_extra": {}, so the read raises KeyError. The read sits before the PROBE_KIND branch, so both classifier and generator eval stages fail; the CPU-stage path then appends a failed finish row and stops the walk, blocking every train->eval hand-off. verified.title: A LoRA run cannot resume: base.load on a ckpt_dir builds no adapter, so the optimizer state does not load and the resumed run would fine-tune everything
verified.detail: trainer.run's resume path calls base.load(..., ckpt_dir=run_dir/'last', ...) and then rebuilds AdamW over probe.trainable_parameters() and calls opt.load_state_dict(torch.load(last/optimizer.pt)["opt"]). base.load only builds the peft wrapper when ckpt_dir is None (base.py:215-216), so a restored probe has lora=None: Probe.trainable_parameters returns every backbone and head parameter instead of the LoRA parameters the pre-crash optimizer held, and AdamW.load_state_dict rejects the mismatch. Even if the state load were skipped, the resumed incarnation would full-fine-tune a run whose frozen probe.tuning says lora, and save() would keep writing full weights. This is GPU item 3 crossed with GPU item 5 of ticket 13; the reports record the resume gap about the best objective, not this.
verified.repro:
/tmp/seams/lora_resume.py reproduces the two parameter sets with the tickets' tiny two-layer Qwen3 and the real peft config from base.py:
  tuning=lora, first launch: optimizer holds 30 tensors
  tuning=lora, after resume: optimizer holds 26 tensors
  trainer.py:223 opt.load_state_dict -> ValueError: loaded state dict contains a parameter group that doesn't match the size of optimizer's group

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED. I reproduced it on CPU with the real models/probe_models/base.py and a tiny two-layer Qwen3 (/tmp/seams6_repro.py, run under external/probe-env): with probe.tuning=lora the fresh probe's trainable_parameters() holds 30 tensors (28 LoRA + 2 head); probe.save writes merged full weights with no adapter_* file (meta.tuning still reads "lora", which is what ticket 13 GPU item 5 prescribes); base.load(..., ckpt_dir=last) then returns a probe with lora=None and 26 trainable tensors, and torch.optim.AdamW.load_state_dict(saved["opt"]) raises "ValueError: loaded state dict contains a parameter group that doesn't match the size of optimizer's group". The identical control under tuning=full loads cleanly (26 -> 26). This is precisely trainer.run's resume sequence: trainer.py:176-177 (base.load with ckpt_dir=run_dir/"last"), :211 (AdamW over probe.trainable_parameters()), :223 (opt.load_state_dict), with last/optimizer.pt always written beside probe.save at :296-300, so the resume path always finds the file. Consequence: a LoRA run that survives one checkpoint_hours boundary and is then restarted dies instead of resuming, and run.py retry (start fresh) is the only way forward.

Against the requirements: contracts 2.4 and ticket 13 step 3 state that last/ with a matching commit means "resume from last/meta.json[step]", with no exemption for a tuning value; errata line 110 gives optimizer.pt its home in last/ precisely so the resume restores it. No ticket line or errata entry prescribes this failure. base.py itself is doing what ticket 06 pins ("ckpt_dir restores: weights and tokenizer from that directory (LoRA was merged at save time, so a restore is a plain from_pretrained)"), and errata line 115 bars peft from trainer.py, so neither file can be called non-compliant in isolation -- the two pinned interfaces meet in a gap, and the wave-5 code is where a contracted path stops working. The secondary claim in the finding (the resumed incarnation would full-fine-tune a run whose frozen probe.tuning says lora, with save() writing full weights) is correct as a consequence but only materialises if the optimizer state load is skipped, e.g. optimizer.pt missing; at HEAD the loud ValueError comes first.

Not a duplicate of what is recorded: T13-report.md (lines 142, 281, 353) and wave-result.json record only the best-objective resume gap; wave-result.json line 33 records as an unverified limitation that base.py's real load/save behaviour was never exercised from trainer.py. This finding is the confirmed failure inside that unchecked area, i.e. strictly worse than what is on record.

Severity important rather than critical: no settings file currently writes probe.tuning: lora (experimental_settings/schema.py carries only the default "full" and the axis ("full", "lora")), and the failure is a hard ValueError rather than silent corruption, so nothing running today is damaged. It matters because LoRA is the tuning used for the bigger backbones whose runs last tens of hours, checkpoint_hours defaults to 2.0, and GPU item 3 (resume) is run with the default full tuning, so nothing in the acceptance set would catch it. The fix is an owner-level call (re-wrap the adapter after a restore inside base.load, or store the adapter plus optimizer state in last/), not a trainer.py-only edit.

verified.title: A checkpoint restored on a GPU comes back in bfloat16, which crashes the generator forward and silently changes a classifier's training dtype
verified.detail: base.load picks `row["dtype"]` (float32 for every probe row in models/table.yaml) on a fresh load but `backbone_module.DTYPE` (bfloat16) whenever ckpt_dir is set and device starts with cuda. Feeding that last-before-finish beat to jobs.registry.judge with alive True and beat_age_s 3600 returns ('done', False), confirming jobs/registry.py:662.

Why it is not a defect against the governing text:
1. Ticket 13 (.scratch/from-zero/issues/13-training-loop-and-probe-methods.md) lists every heartbeat call: step 2 registry.beat, step 9 hb.emit(0, steps, 'step') plus one every LOG_EVERY steps, step 10 "hb.emit is called during a long validation so the stall line is not crossed", step 13 hb.finish(). Step 12, the prediction step, prescribes no beat. The rule the finding invokes is written for validation alone, and the code applies it exactly where it is written.
2. Contract 8.4 fixes train's unit as 'step' and one beat per unit of work, so total is the optimizer-step count; when the step loop ends, done == total is a true statement about the counted unit, and any conforming implementation reaches it (the LOG_EVERY beat alone hits it whenever steps is a multiple of 50). Changing the verdict would mean redefining what train's total counts, a contract change rather than a ticket-13 implementation choice.
3. Contract 8.5 itself pins the priority order with done first: "done when status == done or done >= total". registry.judge implements the contract's own ranking. None of the last ten errata entries touches this; errata 155 only fixes eval's total, and contracts 9(d) leaves "the cost of predicting at every cut row" as an undecided quantity to be measured.
4. Nothing automated reads the premature 'done' verdict. jobs/launch.gate_open_row (launch.py:222-266) refuses on a live session, a fresh heartbeat or the launch timeout, and the tmux session is live throughout predict, so the key stays gated; registry.cards_busy marks the card busy from session liveness; run.py's walk skips a train stage on done.json existing (run.py:711), written after predict; registry.sync (registry.py:988-1027) acts on done.json or on all-pieces-dead, never on a 'done' verdict. The effect is confined to the pieces column of run.py ls, where the row's own status still reads 'launching' and no finish row exists.
5. The ticket's GPU item 7, cited as the reason the phase must be observable, measures it as "(done.json mtime - train_done.json mtime) / predictions rows" -- by file mtimes, not by beats.

Residual observation, neither a ticket-13 defect nor worse than what the wave-5 reports record: on 2.4's predict-only continue path the trainer emits no beat at all before the prediction loop, so that incarnation's file is empty until finish() writes {done 0,total 0,unit '',status done} and judge reads 'warming up' then 'suspected stall' -- the opposite symptom, and a question about contract 8.4's wording ("emits emit(0, total, unit) before its main loop") rather than about this merge.
